newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE potentially another Hong Kong - U.S. economist.
newsitem.headline: UAE potentially another Hong Kong - U.S. economist.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates could become another Hong Kong or Singapore but first it needs to build financial services and develop a fiscal strategy, a U.S. economist said on Sunday.

"There is room for a major entrepot economy in the region... The most promising path to sustained high levels of income will come by achieving Dubai's potential as the entrepot of the region," said Jeffrey Sachs, director of the Harvard Institute for International Development.
Like the world's most competitive economies Singapore and Hong Kong, the UAE, of which Dubai is a member, had made remarkable progress to becoming a dynamic regional trading hub, he said.
But the oil-rich state needed a more sophisticated financial sector to meet the demands of the fast-developing region, Sachs told the annual Emirates International Forum.
"The financial market development has not been able to achieve the full level of growth as has trade and tourism," he said, adding the Gulf still relied largely on London as its financial centre.
"It seems clear this region needs an internationally integrated first-class stock exchange," he said, adding Gulf markets were relatively illiquid and lacked depth.

One reason for Singapore and Hong Kong's success in achieving annual per capita incomes of around $30,000 without significant natural resources was the "enormous synergy" across sectors of the economy, including trade, tourism, education, financial services and financial management, Sachs said.
But the core of the success of an entrepot economy was macro-economic stability "which means a broad, creative, detailed fiscal strategy", he added.
Maintenance of low tax rates and currency stability would help the UAE develop as an entrepot, but there was room for improving the management of risk, particularly in the oil sector, Sachs said.
There was also work needed on a more secure regulatory environment in the Gulf, laying down firm technical and physical infrastructure and developing human resources.
Sachs has advised Russia, many Latin American and East European nations on restructuring their economies.
